title: The Road to the Old Market

before.title: The Road to the Old Market

This story is set long ago. A road goes from a village to the sea.

A woman walks along it with a basket. She has eggs to sell. A man has cloth in his cart.

They stop by a well. Then they go on together. The market is not far now.

title: A Sailor Reads the Stars

before.title: A Sailor Reads the Stars
before.text: A sailor stood on a wooden ship at night. There were no road signs on the sea. He found a bright star in the north and kept it on his left. Hour after hour, the ship moved east. At sunrise, land appeared ahead. The stars had not spoken, but their place in the sky had shown him the way.

after.title: A Sailor Reads the Stars
after.text: A sailor stood on a ship at night. He wanted to sail east. He found the North Star. It showed him where north was. He kept that star to his left. The ship moved through the night. At sunrise, he saw land ahead. The star had helped him keep his course.

reason: NASA confirms that Polaris identifies north in the Northern Hemisphere; keeping it left is consistent with an eastward course. Name that setting and mark this particular voyage as invented. Final pass: split dense sentences into short Level 1 clauses and checked the referents.

title: Why Ice Floats

before.title: Why Ice Floats
before.text: Put an ice cube in a glass of water. It stays at the top. Ice is water, but it takes up more space when it becomes hard and cold. This makes ice lighter than the same amount of water. That is why it floats. A lake can freeze on top while fish still swim in water below.

after.title: Why Ice Floats
after.text: Put an ice cube in a glass of water. It floats at the top. Ice is frozen water. When water freezes, it takes up more space. The same weight of ice is spread through more space than liquid water. That is why ice can float. In a cold winter, a lake may freeze on top while there is still liquid water below.

reason: The USGS confirms ice is less dense than liquid water. “Lighter than the same amount” confuses mass with volume; explain that the same weight takes up more space when frozen.

title: The Moving Tree Shadow

before.title: The Moving Tree Shadow
before.text: A tree's shadow is long in the morning. Near the middle of the day, it grows short. In the evening, it becomes long again on the other side. The tree does not move. The sun seems to move across the sky, so its light comes from a new place. The changing light makes the shadow travel over the ground.

after.title: The Moving Tree Shadow
after.text: The shadow of a tree is long in the morning. Near the middle of the day, it grows short. In the evening, it becomes long again on the other side. The tree does not move. The Sun seems to move across the sky. Its light now comes from another place. The changing light makes the shadow move over the ground.

reason: The tree stays in place as the apparent Sun position changes over a sunny day. The morning, middle and evening observations explain the moving shadow without presenting an invented experiment as historical fact. title: Seeds Need Air

before.title: Seeds Need Air
before.text: Two bean seeds went into two jars. One jar had air. The other was full of water. Both seeds had water and warmth, but only the seed with air began to grow well. A seed is not awake like an animal, yet it is alive. It needs air to use the food inside it and start a new plant.

after.title: Seeds Need Air
after.text: A bean seed needs water and warmth to grow. It also needs air. Put a seed in wet soil, and it may start to grow. But too much water can fill the spaces where air would be. Then the seed may not get enough air. A seed is alive. It needs both water and air as a new plant begins to grow.

reason: Seeds generally need oxygen as well as water and warmth, but a submerged seed is not guaranteed to fail because water can contain dissolved oxygen. Replace the absolute two-jar result with a qualified explanation of too much water.
